text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - A Philippine firm bought 40,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at $3.70 to $3.90 a bushel, Manila grain traders said on Monday. Traders said the firm bought 15,000 tonnes of western white wheat at an average $3.70 a bushel FOB U.S. Pacific northwest port. The firm also bought 25,000 tonnes dark northern spring wheat at 14 percent protein content at $3.90 a bushel. The wheat is for delivery this month and next month, they added.

SOYBEAN TENDER - The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association will tender on Tuesday for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans, traders said on Monday. Traders had said the Taichung division's tender was highly likely following Friday's purchase of 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans by an unaffiliated rival, the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association Kaohsiung division. Shipment was slated for April 11-25 if U.S. Gulf or April 26-May 10 if Pacific Northwest.
WHEAT TENDERS - Iraq will tender on March 11 for 50,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat slated for May delivery, several U.S. exporters said.

- Lebanon's economy ministry said on Thursday it would hold a new tender for the purchase on its behalf of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat on international markets next week. Bids would be for two shipments CIF to Beirut port silos of 25,000 tonnes each, the first between April 15 and May 10 and the second between June 20 and July 15.
- Sri Lanka said it would tender for 50,000 tonnes each of hard and soft wheat. The tender will close on March 13.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - The CCC said it was tendering on March 12 to buy up to 15,180 tonnes of U.S. hard red wheat for export to Angola, April 1-25 shipment. CCC said it was seeking no. 2 or better hard red spring or hard red winter wheat.

CORN TENDER - The CCC said it was tendering on March 12 to buy up to 16,080 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn, for export to Angola. CCC said it was seeking No. 2 or better U.S. yellow corn, maximum moisture 14.5 percent, for April 1-25 shipment.

MARKET TALK - South Korean buyers estimate China may have a further half-million tonnes of corn on offer after domestic feedmills embarked on a buying spree, picking up 250,000 tonnes of Chinese origin. Traders said Japanese buyers, who have covered 90 percent of their April/June corn requirements, may also buy Chinese corn soon in place of U.S. grain...The European Union may wrap up soft wheat exports for the 1996/97 campaign before the traditional end-April deadline, having already exported substantial volumes, an EU Commission official said.

MARKET TALK (cont.) - Pakistan is likely to tender for at least 100,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat this month, the U.S. agriculture attache in Islamabad said on Monday. The attache said the tender, which had originally been expected on March 16, could now be issued on March 23...Spain's wheat crop in the southern region of Andalusia may be substantially lower this year because of damage and sowing delays during floods, a spokesman for a regional farmers' group said...Thailand does not plan to fully liberalise corn imports just yet as lower foreign product prices would hurt local farmers, Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said Monday.
